title: Core passes its tests on Windows x86_64
goal: Every core release since v0.21.55 is qualified on Linux only and owes Windows x86_64. A Windows run of the release gates (release/2026-11-11-rc3, then main 71b5e9651) failed tests that pass on Linux. Fix each at its root: (1) audit chain appends from several processes were refused ('audit chain lock unavailable') because each holder syncs two files to disk (~0.1 s on Windows) and queued writers outlasted the default 3 s lock wait; appends now wait up to 30 s, still failing closed past it; (2) plain_http reported a raw 'connected party did not properly respond' error instead of its time-budget error because Windows socket timers fire a few ms before the deadline; (3) worktree_admin::forget never matched a removed checkout whose path was spelled with 8.3 short names or another case than Windows Git's gitdir record, leaving the dead record behind; (4) the installer contract fixtures used `ln -s`, which Git Bash turns into a copy that cannot load its MSYS runtime DLL; (5) check-hermetic-tests.sh needed jq, absent on a vanilla Windows host; (6) two xtask tests compared an 8.3 short TEMP path with Git's long form as strings.
acceptance: On x86_64-pc-windows-msvc: susi-sandbox-client audit_chain_tests, susi-core plain_http tests, susi tests installer_contract and hermetic_scope, and xtask local-workflow, local-snapshot and worktree_admin tests pass (each failed before)
The same suites still pass on Linux (the changes are portable: canonical-path comparison, exec wrappers instead of symlinks, sed instead of jq)
